missed_issues: Table 9's 'original' value of 0.82 matches the Figure 2 AUROC (0.82), not the 0.80 F1 in Table 1. So Table 9 is most likely AUROC, as its caption says, and the adaptive-attack floor of 0.62 is an AUROC close to chance (0.5). F1 under adaptive attack is effectively unreported, which weakens the 'holds' framing beyond the labelling inconsistency.

The utility evaluation in Table 3 uses 'Before' baselines of 100.00 (HumanEval Pass@1, RepoBench EM and BLEU-4). This implies the sanitized code is scored against the unsanitized or reference code, not against a downstream LLM's task success. End-to-end completion utility after sanitization is never measured, and the abstract and conclusion omit the -32.67 EM cost.

The ASR success criterion is never defined: there is no oracle or judge description across six heterogeneous attack families, and Table 2 compares only no-defense against CodeSentinel on the hosted models.

Leave-one-attack-out (Table 8) shows exactly 0.000 change on three of six families, and Flashboom improves (+0.075) when it is held out of threshold selection. That pattern is hard to reconcile with real held-out tuning. The 'modest average drop' (-0.037) hides drops of -0.127 and -0.140 on the semantic-rewrite families (XOXO, ITGen).
Table 7's targeted setting optimizes attacks against DePA, not against CodeSentinel, so the smaller CodeSentinel drop is favourable by construction.

The RQ2 heading says 'all three layers are necessary', but the evidence is a cumulative ablation on an unspecified 'ablation subset' (Fig. 3). Figure 9 says Layer 3 alone is strongest, and no Layer-3-only versus full-pipeline F1 is reported.
note: I agree with the verdict, the claim strengths and the P22 supports stance. The paper measures defended versus undefended ASR and beats three prior defenses on node-level F1 and DePA on transferred ASR. The added caveats are that the adaptive-attack table is probably AUROC near chance, utility is measured against the reference code rather than downstream task success, and the ASR oracle is undefined.
